details:
The Interplanetary Survival Guide — Martian Map is an interactive 3D Mars globe that reframes scattered Mars data around one human question: where could a person survive, and what should they avoid?

What it does / how it works. Mars is rendered as a clean "planet in space" using live NASA Mars Trek imagery — the Viking colorized global mosaic with MOLA relief — against a starfield. Eight real sites carry clickable space-element markers: rover landings (Jezero/Perseverance, Gale/Curiosity), a historic landing (Viking 1 at Chryse), a candidate crewed base (Arcadia Planitia), and natural landmarks (Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Hellas, the north polar ice cap). Clicking a marker — or picking it from the sites list — flies the camera in and opens an information card with mission quick-facts and a Survival Report assembled from Mars datasets: nearest water-ice and its distance, a hazard rating derived from slope/dust-storm/cold data, resource hints, and temperature. A guided tour steps through all eight sites, and an About panel explains the data and method. The app is a static single-page site with no backend: a data provider prefers live sources and falls back to bundled samples, so it runs even offline, and any missing value is shown honestly as "data unavailable" rather than guessed.

Benefits & intended impact. It turns raw planetary datasets into an intuitive, story-driven survivability view — useful for public outreach, education, and building quick intuition about mission sites — and provides a foundation for plugging in richer live NASA data.

Tools & tech. TypeScript + Vite; CesiumJS for the 3D globe, camera fly-to, and surface markers; NASA Mars Trek tile services for imagery/relief; Vitest + fast-check for testing (66 tests, including property-based tests of the core geodesy, hazard, and report logic); deployed on Vercel. Marker icons are hand-authored SVG vector art.

Creativity. Rather than dumping data layers on a map, it models a modern interactive viewer: marker → cinematic fly-in → facts + survival report, so exploration becomes a narrative. The survival report is computed from pure, testable functions (nearest-neighbour geodesy on the Mars radius, a monotonic hazard rule), making the assessment transparent and reproducible.

Factors we considered. Demo reliability (fallback-everywhere so no network failure blanks it), honesty (explicit "data unavailable" instead of fabricated numbers), performance (lightweight static build), and accessibility of the data (public NASA Mars Trek sources, no token required).
